title: Framer is now in Cursor
how: ffmpeg streamed the video from its URL into cutscene's measure (256 px luma, every frame); nothing saved but these numbers and stills in scratch
whyTopTier: A 16 s partnership launch that starts in live action, overhead hands typing on a laptop, and dissolves into the prompt being typed on screen. A slow pull then frames the prompt's panel, and the result is a CMS table updating row by row. 8 shots, still only 39%.
instrument: 24 fps. The clean fit is the pull from the typed prompt back to its panel: ×0.58 over 2.3 s, ease-out (rms 1.7%; cutscene's in-out 11.8%). The other long moves cross dissolves.

byEye.zoom: the prompt at about ×3, then pulled to ×1.7; the result table wide
byEye.cards: 'Framer is now in Cursor'; the Cursor × Framer lockup
byEye.sound: an audio track with rhythmic onsets (not listened to)

classify: Hybrid launch film (live action into screen) for an integration. Conventions: hands on keys, a typed prompt, one result shot, a card, an 'A × B' lockup.

diagnose.observation: Hands typing dissolve into text arriving in the prompt.
diagnose.principle: Match on action: the typing carries across the cut, so the on-screen text reads as typed by a person.

diagnose.observation: The pull from the prompt runs 2.3 s with an ease-out curve.
diagnose.principle: Out-family deceleration on a reveal: the frame opens fast and settles, which reads as a camera, not a UI transition.

diagnose.observation: Rows highlight one after another in the result.
diagnose.principle: A batch change shown as a sweep (stagger), so 'many rows updated' is seen, not stated.

diagnose.observation: The card holds 4.6 s, over a quarter of the film.
diagnose.principle: The partnership is the news, so the card gets the longest hold.

teaches.text: A reveal pull can run 2–2.3 s on an out curve.
Typing close-up at ×3, then pull to context once the line is complete.
Hand typing over to the screen: a key-cap or keyboard insert that cuts to the text arriving.

critique.like: Cutting from hands to the prompt carries the typing across the cut, so the prompt feels authored.
critique.wish: The result shot is dark and small; the rows changing are hard to read at feed size.
critique.wonder: Could act.type open on a key-cap overlay that hands off to the on-screen text in one cut?
